title: Generating set-cogenerated cotorsion pairs: smallness and filtrations
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] in a fixed universe, $S$ a set of objects, $\mathcal T=S^{\perp_1}$, and $\mathcal L={}^{\perp_1}\mathcal T$. Here $\operatorname{Ext}^1(U,V)=0$ means that every short exact sequence $0\to V\to E\to U\to0$ splits; the orthogonals require this against every object of the given class. Suppose $G\in\mathcal L$ is a generator, meaning every object is an epimorphic image of a small coproduct of copies of $G$.
Then $(\mathcal L,\mathcal T)$ is a complete cotorsion pair: $\mathcal T=\mathcal L^{\perp_1}$, and every object $X$ occurs in short exact sequences $0\to T\to L\to X\to0$ and $0\to X\to T'\to L'\to0$ with $L,L'\in\mathcal L$ and $T,T'\in\mathcal T$. There is a set $I$ of monomorphisms, each with cokernel isomorphic to an object of $S\cup\{G\}$, whose right lifting class is exactly the epimorphisms with kernel in $\mathcal T$. Right lifting means every commutative square with a left map in $I$ admits a diagonal filler. Moreover $\mathcal L$ consists exactly of retracts of $S\cup\{G\}$-filtered objects. An $S\cup\{G\}$-filtered object is the colimit of a small ordinal-indexed continuous increasing chain of subobjects starting at zero, with each successor quotient isomorphic to an object of $S\cup\{G\}$; continuity means that at a limit ordinal the subobject is the colimit of the preceding subobjects. A retract has maps $X\to Y\to X$ with composite $1_X$. No enough-projectives hypothesis is required.

source.place: Agent-formulated generic smallness/filtration tool for proof paragraph 2. WANTED: Saorin and Stovicek, On exact categories and applications to triangulated adjoints and model structures, arXiv:1005.3248v2, Proposition 2.7, Theorem 2.13 and Corollary 2.15; Gillespie, A Quillen Approach to Derived Categories and Tensor Products, arXiv:math/0607769, Lemma 3.4. Both read online, not archived. No Stacks tag states the strongly homological-set construction.

proof.text: Put $S^+=S\cup\{G\}$. By the definition of $\mathcal T$ and $\mathcal L$, $S\subseteq\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal L^{\perp_1}=\mathcal T$: one inclusion follows from $S\subseteq\mathcal L$, and the other from $\mathcal L={}^{\perp_1}\mathcal T$. Since $G\in\mathcal L$, adding $G$ does not change the right orthogonal, so $(S^+)^{\perp_1}=\mathcal T$.

source.place: Agent argument, orthogonal definitions; compare Saorin-Stovicek, Section 1.3, read online.

proof.text: For each $C\in S^+$ and subset $J\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}(G,C)$ whose evaluation $\rho_{C,J}:G^{(J)}\to C$ is epic, choose its kernel $i_{C,J}:K_{C,J}\hookrightarrow G^{(J)}$. Let $I$ consist of all these maps and also $0\to G$. It is a set in the fixed universe: $S^+$ is a set, each Hom is a set, and the power set of each such Hom is a set. Each cokernel is in $S^+$, because in an abelian category an epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel. Coproducts and kernels exist by the cited definitions. Each $C$ has at least one such $J$: an epimorphic coproduct of copies of $G$ onto $C$ factors through the full evaluation indexed by $\operatorname{Hom}(G,C)$, so that evaluation is epic.

source.place: Agent construction after Saorin-Stovicek Proposition 2.7(2), read online; kernels and epimorphisms are used only as in the definition of an abelian category.

proof.text: For any short exact sequence $0\to T\xrightarrow{u}E\xrightarrow{q}C\to0$ with $C\in S^+$, set $J=\{qf:f:G\to E\}\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}(G,C)$. The full evaluation onto $E$ is epic by the generator hypothesis, so its composite with $q$ is epic; this composite factors through $\rho_{C,J}$ by sending each summand indexed by $f$ to the summand indexed by $qf$. Thus $\rho_{C,J}$ is epic. Choose for each $j\in J$ one $f_j:G\to E$ with $qf_j=j$. Their coproduct gives $h:G^{(J)}\to E$ with $qh=\rho_{C,J}$. Since $qhi_{C,J}=0$, the kernel property gives $a:K_{C,J}\to T$ with $ua=hi_{C,J}$. This provides a morphism of short exact sequences with identity on the quotient $C$, for every such extension; no projectivity or lifting of arbitrary maps from $G$ was assumed.

source.place: Agent construction after Saorin-Stovicek Proposition 2.7(2), read online; choices are only among the maps defining J.

proof.text: Suppose $p:X\to Y$ has the right lifting property against $I$. Testing $0\to G$ says every $G\to Y$ lifts to $X$. Choose an epimorphism $G^{(H)}\to Y$; lift its summands and assemble them to factor that epimorphism through $p$, proving $p$ epic. Write $k:T\hookrightarrow X$ for its kernel. For $i:A\to B$ in $I$ and $a:A\to T$, apply lifting to the square with top $ka$ and bottom $0:B\to Y$. Its filler $d:B\to X$ satisfies $pd=0$, so factors through $k$ and extends $a$. Consequently every map from the domain of any map in $I$ to $T$ extends across that map.

source.place: Agent argument; Saorin-Stovicek Lemma 2.2(2), read online, with the pullback calculation written via kernels.

proof.text: Apply the preceding extension property to the map $a:K_{C,J}\to T$ of step 3, obtaining $r:G^{(J)}\to T$ with $ri_{C,J}=a$. Then $h-ur$ vanishes on $K_{C,J}$ and factors through its cokernel $\rho_{C,J}$ as $s:C\to E$. Since $q(h-ur)=\rho_{C,J}$ and $\rho_{C,J}$ is epic, $qs=1_C$. Thus every extension of each $C\in S^+$ by $T$ splits, and $T\in\mathcal T$.

source.place: Agent argument after Saorin-Stovicek Lemma 2.5, read online; the explicit difference h-ur replaces any uncited pushout or extension theorem.

proof.text: Conversely, let $p:X\to Y$ be epic with kernel $T\in\mathcal T$. For each $i\in I$, its cokernel belongs to $S^+$ and hence is Ext-orthogonal to $T$ by step 1. Apply the lifting clause of [lem-coef-cotorsion-orthogonality-calculus] to $i$ and $p$; it gives a filler in every square. Therefore $I^{\square}$ is exactly the epimorphisms with kernel in $\mathcal T$.

source.place: Agent argument using the existing generic orthogonality/lifting node; compare Saorin-Stovicek Lemma 2.5.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-grothendieck-locally-presentable], $\mathcal A$ is locally presentable in the same universe. Apply [lem-coef-presentable-cellular-factorization] to the set $I$ of step 2. Every map $f$ factors as $f=pj$, with $p\in I^{\square}$ and $j$ a continuous small ordinal composite of pushouts of small coproducts of maps of $I$. The cited factorization explicitly supplies the cellular form of $j$, not merely a left lifting property.

source.place: Agent use of cellular small-object factorization; Saorin-Stovicek Proposition 2.1, read online, and the locally-presentable input.

proof.text: We now turn the cellular map $j:X\to Z$ of step 7 into a chain with single-cell successor quotients. At one stage, well-order the attaching set $T$ and write its maps as $i_t:A_t\to B_t$. If the stage starts at $V$, with attaching map $\bigoplus_t A_t\to V$, define $V_\beta=V\amalg_{\bigoplus_{t<\beta}A_t}\bigoplus_{t<\beta}B_t$. The coproduct and pushout universal properties identify $V_0=V$, the final $V_\beta$ with the original simultaneous attachment, and each successor with the pushout of the single map $i_\beta$; at limits the same universal properties give the colimit of preceding stages. We use monicity only for these refined single-cell successor maps: each is monic by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-pushout-mono], with cokernel $\operatorname{Coker}(i_\beta)\in S^+$ by [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-cokernel-iso]. Thus no exactness or monicity assertion for a coproduct of the $i_t$ is needed. Concatenate these small ordinal refinements over the original small ordinal. At a limit, exact filtered colimits preserve the monomorphisms from every fixed earlier stage: apply exactness to the chains $0\to V_\alpha\to V_\gamma$ for $\gamma\geq\alpha$. Thus the full chain consists of subobjects and $j$ is monic. Quotient its terms by the initial $X$: at successors the quotient-of-quotient universal property leaves the same successor cokernel, and at limits exact filtered colimits applied to $0\to X\to V_\gamma\to V_\gamma/X\to0$ give continuity. Hence $Z/X$ is $S^+$-filtered; when $X=0$, $Z$ itself is $S^+$-filtered.

source.place: Agent refinement and quotient argument; Stacks 08N4 (lemma-cartesian-cocartesian), 08N3 (lemma-cartesian-kernel), and exact filtered colimits from the Grothendieck definition.

proof.text: Every $S^+$-filtered object $F$ belongs to $\mathcal L$. Indeed, take $T\in\mathcal T$ and any extension $0\to T\to E\xrightarrow{q}F\to0$. For its continuous filtration $F_\alpha$, construct compatible maps $s_\alpha:F_\alpha\to E$ with $qs_\alpha$ the inclusion in $F$. Start with the zero map. At a successor apply [lem-coef-cotorsion-orthogonality-calculus] to $F_\alpha\hookrightarrow F_{\alpha+1}$ and $q$: the cokernel lies in $S^+$ and its Ext against $\operatorname{Ker}(q)=T$ vanishes. The filler extends $s_\alpha$. At each limit the colimit property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] defines the compatible map, whose composite with $q$ remains the inclusion because it agrees on all preceding terms. The final map is a section of $q$. Thus $F\perp_1T$ for every $T\in\mathcal T$.

source.place: Agent transfinite lifting proof; compare Saorin-Stovicek Proposition 2.12, read online. All successor lifting is supplied by the cited node, all limit lifting by the colimit definition.

proof.text: Apply step 7 to $0\to X$: it gives $0\to T\to F\to X\to0$, where the right map is epic with kernel $T\in\mathcal T$ by steps 4-6, and $F$ is $S^+$-filtered by step 8, hence belongs to $\mathcal L$ by step 9. Apply it to $X\to0$: step 8 gives a monomorphism $X\to T'$ with $S^+$-filtered cokernel $F'$, and steps 4-6 give $T'\in\mathcal T$ because the kernel of $T'\to0$ is $T'$. Thus $0\to X\to T'\to F'\to0$ is the other required sequence, with $F'\in\mathcal L$. Together with step 1 this proves completeness.

source.place: Agent substitution into the cellular factorization already proved in steps 7-9; compare Saorin-Stovicek Theorem 2.13(4)-(5).

proof.text: If $X\in\mathcal L$, its first sequence from step 10 splits since its kernel is in $\mathcal T$. A section $X\to F$ and the epimorphism $F\to X$ exhibit $X$ as a retract of the $S^+$-filtered object $F$. Conversely, a retract of an $S^+$-filtered object belongs to $\mathcal L$ by step 9 and the retract-closure clause of [lem-coef-cotorsion-orthogonality-calculus]. This proves the final characterization. No step used enough projectives.
